title: Post-Course Portfolio: Online Quiz Platform
descriptionMarkdown:
# Online Quiz Platform

## Position in the curriculum

Post-course portfolio: build after finishing the full curriculum through the final capstone, and after (or alongside) the Authentication & User Management System, since scoring an authenticated user's attempt is this project's central requirement, not an afterthought bolted on at the end.

## What is graded, and what is external

This project has a dedicated, automatically-graded checkpoint: **`quiz-scoring-checkpoint`** ("Idempotent quiz scorer"), a pure in-memory `QuizScorer.run(String input)` program implementing exactly the define/submit/score/idempotent-resubmission core. Passing its hidden tests proves your scoring and duplicate-detection rules are correct, independent of any real authentication or persistence.

Wiring this logic to real authenticated users and a real database is external and self-reviewed. Reuse the Authentication & User Management System's login/authorization component directly rather than reimplementing it.

## Architecture overview

```text
QuizController               <- POST /api/quizzes/{id}/attempts, GET leaderboard
QuizService                   <- your checkpoint's scoring/idempotency rules, reshaped as a Spring bean
Quiz / Question / Choice (JPA entities)
Attempt (JPA entity)           <- user, quiz, submitted answers, score, idempotency key, @Transactional boundary
```

## Build it as vertical slices

1. **Slice 1 — port the checkpoint logic into a service.** Carry your define/submit/score/duplicate-detection rules into `QuizService`, unit tests unchanged.
2. **Slice 2 — the JPA schema.** `Quiz`/`Question`/`Choice` entities; ensure the correct-choice flag is never included in any DTO served before submission.
3. **Slice 3 — the submission endpoint, transactionally.** Wrap scoring and persisting the attempt's answer rows in one transaction; force a mid-write failure in a test and confirm no partial attempt is recorded.
4. **Slice 4 — real authentication and object-level authorization.** Reuse the Authentication project's login; a user may only view their own attempt history.
5. **Slice 5 — the leaderboard.** `GET /api/quizzes/{id}/leaderboard` returning top scores, computed with a database aggregate query, not by loading every attempt into memory.

## Common pitfalls

- **Trusting a client-submitted score instead of recomputing it server-side.** The checkpoint's own contract computes the score from the submitted answers every time; never accept a score value from the request body at all.
- **Making the submission endpoint retry-unsafe.** A network retry of an identical submission must produce the same recorded attempt and score, never a second one — exactly your checkpoint's DUPLICATE handling, now backed by a real unique constraint on (quiz, attempt) in the database as a second line of defense.
- **Leaking the correct-answer flag in the questions payload.** Test this explicitly by inspecting the raw JSON served before any submission.
- **Computing the leaderboard by fetching every attempt into Java and sorting there.** Use `ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT n` at the database level instead.

## How to self-test what the checkpoint cannot reach

- Submit an attempt, then replay the exact same HTTP request (same body) and confirm the response and recorded score are identical, not doubled.
- Inspect the raw JSON of an unattempted quiz's questions (via `curl`) and confirm no field reveals which choice is correct.
- Force a failure partway through persisting a multi-question attempt (a deliberate exception in a test) and confirm no partial attempt row exists afterward.

## Required evidence

- A scoring test suite covering all-correct, all-incorrect, partially-correct, and an attempt that omits an answer to one question.
- A test proving the correct-choice flag is never present in the JSON served for an unattempted quiz's questions.
- An idempotency test: submitting the identical attempt payload twice (simulating a retried request) produces one recorded attempt and one score, not two.
- A transaction rollback test: a failure while persisting the attempt's answer rows leaves no partial attempt recorded.
- An authorization test confirming a user can only view their own attempt history, not another user's, using the object-level check from the Authentication project.

## Review and completion

A reviewer retries the exact same submission request twice in quick succession (simulating a flaky network client) and expects one attempt, one score, and no error on the second call — then inspects the response payload for any question the user has not yet attempted and confirms no correct-answer data ever leaked into it.
learningObjectives: Complete the graded idempotent quiz scorer checkpoint and carry its verified rules into a real, authenticated Spring Boot service
Compute and persist a score entirely server-side, never trusting a client-submitted value
Make a scored submission endpoint idempotent against a retried request
Prevent a correct-answer field from ever leaking into a response served before submission
Reuse an existing authentication/authorization component rather than reimplementing login for a new project
